title: R’ Yehudah bar Titus
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A student of R’ Acha, in whose name he reported: Berakhot, chapter 3, halakhah 4; Sukkah, chapter 8, halakhah 8. In Shabbat, chapter 13, halakhah 2: R’ Yehudah bar Titus, R’ Yehudah ben Pazi, Shimon bar Ba, in the name of R’ Yochanan. In Bikkurim, chapter 3, end of halakhah 3, Hyman says that he needed to go to Rome, and they ordained him provisionally, on condition that he return to the Land of Israel; R’ Chama called him Yehudah bar Titas. Among those reporting in his name, we find the rabbis of Caesarea in Gittin, chapter 5, halakhah 10, and Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, halakhah 3. Knesset HaGedolah on Yoreh Deah cites the book Tamim Deim as saying that it should read R’ Yehudah ben Antigonus: how could a Jew be called Titus? It seems more likely that it should read R’ Yehudah bar Sitos, as at the end of Sheviit, chapter 5, and that a samekh was mistakenly made into a tet.

notes.text: The checked Bikkurim says that Yehudah ben Titus was in Rome and was ordained on condition of return, while Hyman says he needed to go there. The supplied Sukkah 8:8 reference is also irregular. Titus/Antigonus/Sitos are proposed textual alternatives, not new identity bindings.

Every personal title in the supplied source is abbreviated and stays R-prime, including the contextual ר״י occurrences; untitled Shimon bar Ba gains none. The Shabbat names are juxtaposed without connectors, so the translation does not impose a complete transmission chain or independent co-reporting. Hyman says the subject needed to go to Rome and was ordained provisionally on condition of returning to the Land of Israel; the earlier reported Bikkurim account places Yehudah ben Titus already in Rome, an inherited discrepancy, not a new whole witness inspection. Sukkah פ״ח ה״ח remains supplied chapter 8 halakhah 8 and unresolved; the earlier bounded Venice nonmatch is not a new or global absence claim. End of Bikkurim halakhah 3 is distinct from end of chapter 3; Sheviit is end of chapter 5. Knesset HaGedolah and Yoreh Deah are contextual work expansions. The cited Tamim Deim should-read Antigonus proposal and its rhetorical question remain attributed. The final more-likely SHOULD READ Sitos proposal and samekh-to-tet history are not adopted; whether Hyman or the cited book owns the final proposal remains open. Titus/Titas, Antigonus and Sitos stay distinct; all source holds remain.

Hyman’s printed page gives Sukkah 8:8. In the consulted Jerusalem Sukkah 5:8 Yehudah ben Titus reports in Acha’s name. The consulted Bikkurim 3:3 places him already in Rome and makes the ordination conditional on his return, while Hyman says he needed to go there and was ordained provisionally. The Caesarean reports occur in the consulted Jerusalem Gittin 5:10 and Avodah Zarah 2:3. The consulted final halakhah of Sheviit chapter 5 reads Titus. The Antigonus and Sitos readings and the proposed letter change remain textual suggestions in the entry. The exact cited Tamim Deim and Knesset HaGedolah passages have yet to be collated.
